defmodule MessageQueue.Consumer do
  @moduledoc """
  Consumes messages from a queue and writes processed results to disk.
  Uses environment-dependent configuration for output paths.
  """

  use GenServer
  require Logger

  defstruct [:queue_name, :output_dir, :processing_mode, :link_policy]

  def start_link(opts) do
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: __MODULE__)
  end

  @impl true
  def init(opts) do
    queue_name = Keyword.get(opts, :queue_name, "default")
    output_dir = resolve_output_directory()
    processing_mode = System.get_env("MQ_PROCESSING_MODE", "batch")
    link_policy = resolve_link_policy()

    state = %__MODULE__{
      queue_name: queue_name,
      output_dir: output_dir,
      processing_mode: processing_mode,
      link_policy: link_policy
    }

    ensure_output_directory(state)
    schedule_consume()
    {:ok, state}
  end

  @impl true
  def handle_info(:consume, state) do
    case fetch_messages(state.queue_name) do
      {:ok, messages} ->
        Enum.each(messages, fn msg -> process_message(msg, state) end)
      {:error, reason} ->
        Logger.error("Failed to fetch messages: #{inspect(reason)}")
    end

    schedule_consume()
    {:noreply, state}
  end

  defp resolve_output_directory do
    base = System.get_env("MQ_OUTPUT_BASE", "/var/lib/mq_consumer")
    env_suffix = System.get_env("MQ_ENV", "production")
    Path.join(base, env_suffix)
  end

  defp resolve_link_policy do
    # In development, we follow symlinks for convenience (mounted volumes, etc.)
    # In production, we use a stricter policy
    case System.get_env("MQ_ENV", "production") do
      "development" -> :follow
      "staging" -> :follow
      "production" -> :verify_then_follow
      _ -> :verify_then_follow
    end
  end

  defp ensure_output_directory(state) do
    File.mkdir_p!(state.output_dir)
  end

  defp process_message(%{id: id, payload: payload, topic: topic}, state) do
    filename = sanitize_filename("#{topic}_#{id}.dat")
    target_path = Path.join(state.output_dir, filename)

    case validate_write_target(target_path, state) do
      :ok ->
        write_processed_output(target_path, payload, state)
      {:error, reason} ->
        Logger.warn("Skipping write to #{target_path}: #{reason}")
    end
  end

  defp validate_write_target(path, state) do
    # Check if path is within our output directory
    canonical_output = Path.expand(state.output_dir)

    case state.link_policy do
      :follow ->
        # Development mode - just check the path prefix
        if String.starts_with?(Path.expand(path), canonical_output) do
          :ok
        else
          {:error, :path_traversal}
        end

      :verify_then_follow ->
        # Production mode - verify symlink safety
        verify_symlink_safety(path, canonical_output)
    end
  end

  defp verify_symlink_safety(path, canonical_output) do
    # First check: does the expanded path stay within bounds?
    expanded = Path.expand(path)
    unless String.starts_with?(expanded, canonical_output) do
      {:error, :path_traversal}
    else
      # Second check: verify no symlink components in the path
      # We check the PARENT directory, not the file itself (file may not exist yet)
      parent = Path.dirname(path)
      case check_path_components(parent, canonical_output) do
        :safe -> :ok
        :unsafe -> {:error, :symlink_detected}
      end
    end
  end

  defp check_path_components(path, base_dir) do
    # Walk each component of the path relative to base_dir
    relative = Path.relative_to(path, base_dir)
    components = Path.split(relative)

    result = Enum.reduce_while(components, base_dir, fn component, acc ->
      current = Path.join(acc, component)
      case File.lstat(current) do
        {:ok, %File.Stat{type: :symlink}} ->
          # Symlink found - but we resolve it and check if target is still within bounds
          case File.read_link(current) do
            {:ok, link_target} ->
              resolved = Path.expand(link_target, Path.dirname(current))
              if String.starts_with?(resolved, base_dir) do
                {:cont, current}
              else
                {:halt, :unsafe}
              end
            {:error, _} ->
              {:halt, :unsafe}
          end
        {:ok, _} ->
          {:cont, current}
        {:error, :enoent} ->
          # Path doesn't exist yet, that's fine for new files
          {:cont, current}
        {:error, _} ->
          {:halt, :unsafe}
      end
    end)

    case result do
      :unsafe -> :unsafe
      _ -> :safe
    end
  end

  defp write_processed_output(target_path, payload, _state) do
    # TOCTOU window: between validate_write_target and actual write,
    # the file or a parent directory could be replaced with a symlink
    processed = transform_payload(payload)
    File.write!(target_path, processed)
    Logger.info("Wrote processed message to #{target_path}")
  end

  defp transform_payload(payload) when is_binary(payload) do
    :crypto.hash(:sha256, payload) |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  defp transform_payload(payload) do
    payload |> inspect() |> transform_payload()
  end

  defp sanitize_filename(name) do
    name
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/, "_")
    |> String.slice(0, 255)
  end

  defp schedule_consume do
    interval = String.to_integer(System.get_env("MQ_POLL_INTERVAL", "5000"))
    Process.send_after(self(), :consume, interval)
  end

  defp fetch_messages(queue_name) do
    # Simulated queue fetch - in production this would connect to RabbitMQ/SQS/etc.
    {:ok, [
      %{id: :erlang.unique_integer([:positive]), payload: "test_data", topic: queue_name}
    ]}
  end
end

defmodule MessageQueue.Application do
  use Application

  def start(_type, _args) do
    children = [
      {MessageQueue.Consumer, [queue_name: System.get_env("MQ_QUEUE_NAME", "events")]}
    ]

    opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: MessageQueue.Supervisor]
    Supervisor.start_link(children, opts)
  end
end
